name: The Krombach Oak
verified_sources: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Luxembourg,_ch%C3%AAne_Krombach,_parc_Louvigny_(101).jpg (independent field photograph by Commons contributor GilPe, dated 3 January 2020, caption: 'le chene Krombach plante en memoire du botaniste Jean-Henri-Guillaume Krombach (1791-1881)', geotagged in Parc Louvigny)

https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q13103645 (structured record: species Quercus robur, named after Jean-Henri-Guillaume Krombach (Q3460050), a point-in-time value of 1875 whose exact meaning is not confirmed, see note)
access: Free, in Parc Louvigny, a public city park in Ville-Haute; open at all times, no restriction found.
transport: Central Luxembourg City, Ville-Haute, near Villa Louvigny; walkable from the city centre, about 0.5km from the Giant Sequoia of Parc Amelie (lux_005) and the Sycamore of Hollerich (lux_008).
verify_notes: NOT found in the 31 January 2025 official register CSV (no INSPIRE point within several hundred metres, and the Wikidata record carries no register-id property), so this rests on two independent non-register sources: a geotagged Commons field photograph (GilPe, 2020) and Wikidata's structured record. Both agree it is an oak (chene) in Parc Louvigny planted or dedicated in memory of Jean-Henri-Guillaume Krombach, a Luxembourg pharmacist and botanist (1791-1881). Wikidata carries a 'point in time' value of 1875, which would make the tree about 150 years old if it is a planting date, but the property used (P585) does not clearly mean 'planted' rather than some other event date (e.g. when the memorial naming happened), and no source seen states 'planted in 1875' outright. Treating that date as an age would be a bridge claim, so age_estimate is left empty and the date is flagged here for the writer/reader instead. Species confirmed as Quercus robur via Wikidata taxon claim; visually an oak in both photographs. Girth and height not found. id reassigned from lux_004 to lux_010 (2026-08-30 session): the live city already runs lux_001-009, and this was the only one of four candidates in the original pass (filed under the mismatched-name data/research/luxembourgcity-verified.json) that was not already published under a different name: lux_001 duplicated live lux_001 (Robert-Brasseur Chestnut), lux_002 duplicated live lux_003 (Beech of Bastion Beck, identical coordinates), lux_003 duplicated live lux_009 (Sycamore of Pfaffenthal, identical coordinates).
